1. `docs/design-system.md` — binding contract.
2. `app/globals.css` — note a site-wide custom scrollbar was JUST added (search for "SCROLLBAR" near the bottom) using `scrollbar-width`/`scrollbar-color` (Firefox) and `::-webkit-scrollbar*` (Chrome/Safari/Edge), bound to `--border-strong` and `--brand-ring` tokens. 3. `components/ui/Modal.tsx` — the native `<dialog>`-based modal every picker/wizard uses.
4. `components/wizard/InlineWizard.tsx` (~950 lines) — the file you're mainly fixing. Read it in full.
5. `components/wizard/inline-brief.ts`, `components/wizard/inline-logo.ts` — its supporting logic.
6. `components/templates/TemplatePickerModal.tsx` — a sibling component with the SAME kind of multi-stage-in-a-modal structure. Check whether it has the same overflow bug; if so, fix it there too using the same technique for consistency.
7. `lib/features.ts` — the feature library the wizard's Features stage renders from.

YOU OWN: `components/wizard/InlineWizard.tsx`, `components/wizard/inline-brief.ts`, `components/wizard/inline-logo.ts`, `components/templates/TemplatePickerModal.tsx`. Do NOT touch `app/(portal)/dashboard/new/**`, `components/ui/**`, `app/globals.css`, or `lib/features.ts`'s actual feature data (you may read it).

## BUG 1 — the wizard renders outside the modal's frame

Screenshots show the wizard's content (category pills, a scrollbar) overflowing past the visible modal card — the scrollable content area is not properly contained within the dialog's rounded frame, and there's a second independent scrollbar appearing to the right of the whole dialog rather than one scrollbar inside it. Find the actual layout bug: likely a missing `overflow-hidden` on the outer dialog frame, a max-height that isn't being respected by a flex/grid child, or a scroll container that isn't correctly bounded. Fix it so the ENTIRE wizard — header, stage indicator, stage content, footer buttons — renders fully inside one bounded, rounded modal frame, with exactly one internal scroll region for the stage content when it's taller than available space. Verify the same fix (or lack of the same bug) in `TemplatePickerModal.tsx`.

## BUG 2 — the Features stage should be an icon grid, not a scrolling checkbox list

Currently it's a tall list of rows, each with a checkbox and no icon. Redesign it as a responsive grid of icon cards (2–3 columns depending on width), each card showing: an icon, the feature name, its one-line honest description, and a clear selected/unselected state (border + tint change, not just a checkbox — though the checkbox can remain for accessibility). Every feature in `lib/features.ts` (both offered and the `NOT_OFFERED` list, if the stage currently shows both) needs an icon — check what's already there and add `lucide-react` icons for any that are missing a sensible one. Keep every existing honest caveat sentence exactly as strong as it is now (e.g. "Kodely cannot run bookings, availability or payments itself") — do not soften or hide these while making the layout prettier.

## FIX 3 — the logo message is technically true but reads as "your upload does nothing"

The current copy says: "The image file itself can't go on the page — Kodely sites carry no uploaded pictures. The brief asks for a clearly-marked space where your logo goes instead." That's accurate but incomplete, and it currently reads as though the upload is discarded.

**Verify this yourself first**: trace `answers.logo` from where it's set in this file, through `finish()` (`logoDataUrl: answers.logo.dataUrl`), and confirm it actually flows out through `onComplete` and (by reading, not editing) `components/wizard/../new/Composer.tsx`'s `acceptWizard()` and `CreateFlow.tsx`'s `run()` call into the `image` field of `POST /api/generate`. I already traced this and believe it DOES work — the logo really is sent to the model as vision guidance on the first build attempt, exactly like the reference-image path. Confirm that's still true after your other edits, then rewrite the message to say BOTH true things clearly: the actual file can't be embedded in the site, AND Kodely genuinely looks at it to match colours and character in the build, on the first attempt. If your trace finds the pipeline is NOT actually connected (a real bug), fix that instead and say so in your report — do not just take my word for it.

## HARD RULES
- **Never build something that only pretends to work.** Every caveat sentence in the feature library exists because the underlying thing genuinely can't be built (no backend, strict CSP, no image hosting) — do not soften wording to make features look more capable than they are.
- `k-focus` on every interactive element. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Must pass `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint app lib components --max-warnings=0`, zero errors and zero warnings.
- A dev server is running on port 3003 (may need a restart if you change globals-adjacent behavior, but you're not touching globals.css). Try to actually render the modal in a browser if you can reach an authenticated flow; if you can't authenticate, verify via static analysis and be explicit in your report about what's unverified.

REPORT BACK: the exact root cause of the overflow bug and your fix, whether TemplatePickerModal had the same bug, your icon-grid design, what you confirmed about the logo pipeline (verified working, or a real bug you fixed), and anything untested.

50	(`text-ok` / `bg-ok-tint`). Status colour is never the brand colour.
51	
52	### Radius / elevation / motion
53	
54	`rounded-sm|md|lg|xl|2xl` (8/10/14/20/28px) · `shadow-e1|e2|e3` ·
55	`duration-[var(--t-1)]` 120ms, `--t-2` 200ms, `--t-3` 380ms ·
56	`ease-[var(--ease)]`
57	
58	---
59	
60	## Utility classes
61	
62	`k-focus` — **put this on every interactive element.** One focus ring, product-wide.
63	`k-display` `k-h1` `k-h2` `k-label` — the type scale. `k-label` is the only uppercase.
64	`k-num` — **required** on any figure: credits, prices, counts, dates in a column.
65	`k-scroll-x` — wrap any wide table/code block. The page body must never scroll sideways.
66	`k-msg-in` `k-step-in` `k-step-active` — entrance and progress animations.
67	`k-preview-busy` / `k-preview-idle` — the preview treatment while the AI works.
68	`k-wash` — ambient brand glow inside a hero panel. Sparingly: one per page, at most.
69	`k-gradient-border` — gradient hairline. Reserve for the single most important panel.
70	
71	---
72	
73	## Components (`components/ui/`)
74	
75	Import these. **Do not hand-roll a second version of any of them.**
76	
77	| Component | Notes |
78	| --- | --- |
79	| `Button` `ButtonLink` `IconButton` `buttonClass` | Variants `primary\|secondary\|ghost\|soft\|danger`, sizes `xs\|sm\|md\|lg`. **One `primary` per view.** `IconButton` requires `label`. |
80	| `Card` `CardHeader` `SectionHeader` | `interactive` only if it truly responds. |
81	| `Badge` | `tone` + `dot` + `pulse`. Set `dot` on anything conveying live state — colour alone is not a status channel. |
82	| `Input` `Textarea` `Select` `SearchInput` | Label/hint/error/aria wiring is built in. Never hand-write a bare `<input>`. |
83	| `Progress` `toneForUsage` | Recolours as it fills. `indeterminate` for work with no known end. |
84	| `Skeleton` `SkeletonList` | Stagger with `delay`. |
85	| `EmptyState` | `kind` is required: `empty` (none yet) / `no-results` (filter too narrow) / `unavailable` (does not exist yet). These need different sentences. |
86	| `Menu` | Keyboard + Escape + click-outside already handled. `unavailableReason` greys an item and says why. |
87	| `Modal` `ConfirmModal` | Native `<dialog>`. Confirm buttons are labelled with the verb, never "OK". |
88	| `ToastProvider` `useToast` | Provider is already mounted by `AppShell`. Errors and toasts with an action do not auto-dismiss. |
89	| `Segmented` | Real radios. Used for grid/list and device toggles. |
90	| `AIProgress` `stepsAt` | **The** progress component. See below. |
91	| `Stat` `StatRow` | Any number the customer must understand. |
92	| `Avatar` | Initials only — there is no avatar upload. |
93	| `Spinner` | |
94	
95	## Shell (`components/app/`)
96	
97	`AppShell` wraps every portal page and already provides the sidebar, mobile
98	drawer, bottom bar and toast host. **A page renders content only** — no page
99	supplies its own nav, no page sets a background, no page mounts a second
100	`ToastProvider`, and no page sets a title suffix (the group layout owns the
101	`"%s — Kodely"` template; a page declares only its own noun).
102	
103	Navigation lives in `components/app/nav.ts`. An item may only be added there
104	once it is backed by real data; `soon: true` marks the ones that are not.
105	
106	`SidebarFooter` carries the brand-gradient credits card, the theme toggle and
107	the bug/feature link (`/support?topic=bug`, `?topic=feature`). It appears in
108	both the desktop rail and the mobile drawer.
109	
110	**The credits card has no progress bar and no "X of Y" figure, deliberately.**
111	There is no allowance for the balance to be a fraction of — credits are bought
112	in packs and never expire — so a bar would have to invent a denominator. It
113	shows the balance and "about N more builds" from `averageBuildCredits()`.
114	**Anything else in the product showing credits must agree with it.** A card
115	elsewhere claiming a monthly total would contradict the rail sitting beside it.
116	
117	### Where the brand gradient may be used as a fill
118	
119	Three places, and nowhere else: the single `primary` button on a view, the
120	sidebar credits card, and the `/support` credits card. Not on headings, cards,
121	borders, icons or section dividers.
122	
123	---
124	
125	## AI progress is one object, not three spinners
126	
127	`AIProgress` is rendered by the initial build overlay, by the chat panel during
128	an edit, and beside the preview. All three must show the **same steps in the
129	same state**, because the customer reads them as one thing happening.
130	
131	**Drive `state` from real build signals.** A timer that walks the list forward on
132	its own is a fake — and it will still be sitting on "Finalizing" long after a
133	build has failed. The build genuinely does not know its percentage (it is an
134	agent loop of unknown length), which is exactly why this is a named-step list
135	and not a progress bar.
136	
137	---
138	
139	## What does not exist (audited — do not build UI that pretends otherwise)
140	
141	| Thing | Reality |
142	| --- | --- |
143	| **Plans / subscriptions** | None. No plan, price, or renewal date. Checkout is one-off `payment` mode for credit packs. **Never render a "Pro" chip or "$X/month".** |
144	| **Credit reset date** | Credits never expire. There is no monthly allowance and no reset day — the spend cap is a *rolling* 30 days chosen so there is no reset. |
145	| **Invoices / payment method** | Not fetched from Stripe. The credit ledger is the only history. |
146	| **Thumbnails** | Nothing captures a screenshot. No headless browser. |
147	| **Project status** | Only `publishedAt` → Published / Draft. No `archived`. "Building" is derivable from `Build.status = RUNNING` but has no staleness rule, so it is not yet trustworthy. |
148	| **Domains** | No model, no field, no route. Sites live at `<slug>.kodely.site` only. |
149	| **Integrations** | Nothing customer-facing. |
150	| ~~**Support tickets**~~ | **NOW BUILT.** `SupportTicket` + `SupportMessage` exist, with customer-visible staff replies. `SupportNote` remains a separate, admin-only internal note that is still never shown to the customer — do not conflate them. Tickets are included in the data export and the deletion preview; if you add a field holding a customer's words, both must be updated too. |
151	| **Storage / bandwidth** | Not measured anywhere. |
152	| **Workspaces / members / roles** | No concept of it. Ownership is one FK: `Project.userId`. |
153	| **Avatar upload, password change, 2FA, notification prefs** | None. |
154	
155	**Sessions list and revoke, and editing `User.name`, are now BUILT** — see
156	`/settings/security` and `/settings`. Note what `Session` actually records:
157	`id · userId · tokenHash · expiresAt · createdAt`, and nothing else. There is no
158	user agent, no IP, no last-seen and no device. Do not add a column for them
159	casually: `/legal/rights` and the data export both enumerate in writing
160	everything the database holds, so a new personal-data field silently makes two
161	published documents wrong.
162	
163	### The rule
164	
165	A screen that looks operable and is not is worse than an absent one. A screen
166	that says "this does not exist yet, here is what you have instead" is neither.
167	Use `EmptyState kind="unavailable"` and say plainly what is missing.

I'm noticing the modal's dialog element has no max-height set explicitly, relying only on the browser's default UA stylesheet constraints, which could be causing the sizing bug.

Right, `dialog:modal` gets its own `overflow: auto` and `max-height: calc(100% - 6px)` from the UA stylesheet, which means the dialog itself can become a second scroll container independent of any inner scrollable stage content.

That's what's causing the two-scrollbar bug — the outer native dialog scrolling alongside the inner content div when total height exceeds the viewport. The fix is to explicitly override that default with `overflow-hidden` and a constrained `max-h-[...]` on the dialog element itself.

So the actual issue is likely that combined header, rail, stage content and footer height exceeds the viewport, forcing the dialog's own overflow:auto to kick in as a second scrollbar, and depending on the browser, that scroll container's edges may not respect the rounded corners, making content appear to spill past the card's visible boundary.

That mismatch of a second outer scrollbar dragging the whole dialog (header, footer, everything) instead of just the inner content explains the bug — the footer buttons scroll out of view because the dialog's own native overflow is kicking in when total content height exceeds the viewport, especially on shorter screens, rather than the inner container handling the scroll alone.

Since I can't modify Modal.tsx, the real root cause is that the dialog element itself has no max-height/overflow tuned to content, so its default UA overflow kicks in as an outer, unrounded scrollbar competing with my inner intentional one. Actually the browser already clamps dialog:modal to roughly viewport height by default, so the fix in InlineWizard.tsx needs to ensure my content respects that same bound using proper flex sizing so only my inner div scrolls, rather than adding unbounded height that triggers the dialog's own overflow.

But the requirement is exactly one internal scroll region, so I need header, rail, and footer to stay fixed height while only the stage-content div scrolls, with the sum of all fixed sections plus the stage-content's max-height never exceeding the dialog's own max-height. The tricky part is that header/description/rail are variable height — the description can wrap to two lines, and the progress rail wraps on narrow viewports for five stages, potentially adding 100px+ on small screens, which could push the total past the dialog's max-height on short viewports like mobile landscape.

That would trigger the dialog's own overflow:auto behavior, creating a second unwanted scrollbar on the dialog itself. The proper fix within my scope is to make the wizard content a flex column with a fixed header/rail section and a flex-1 min-h-0 overflow-y-auto stage area, though I need to account for how Modal wraps children in a padded div without its own height constraint.

Since I can't modify Modal.tsx, the fix has to live on my side: keep my own content's total height bounded across reasonable viewport widths so it never triggers that outer scroll in the first place, meaning the middle "children" section needs its own constrained scroll area.

The complication is that Modal's own title, description, and footer are rendered outside my controlled div, so I can't include them in my flex layout to manage the overall height budget.

I should also account for the dialog's own default max-height, which is nearly the full viewport minus a few pixels, and sum up title, badges, stage content, and footer heights to make sure the total stays comfortably under that limit.

Actually, rereading the bug description, this might not be a vertical overflow issue at all—the pills overflowing past the modal card sounds like a horizontal problem, where the flex-wrap chip grid isn't properly constrained within the dialog width and spills past its rounded edge, creating a second scrollbar outside the dialog rather than the intended contained scroll region.

I'm reconsidering whether horizontal overflow could really cause something to poke out past the dialog's right edge, but that doesn't fit since the browser's default dialog styling already clips overflow with its own scrollbars—so this explanation doesn't quite match the "second scrollbar to the right" symptom either.

Given the constraints of testing this live in a browser, I'll skip trying to reproduce it interactively and instead dig further into the CSS files, especially the scrollbar-related rules in globals.css, to see if some other overflow interaction explains the issue.

2	 * The feature library — the things a customer can switch ON for their site,
3	 * and the things Kodely will not pretend to offer.
4	 *
5	 * ## Every toggle is a promise about the finished site
6	 *
7	 * A generated site is a real Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind app, built
8	 * server-side and served under
9	 *
10	 *   default-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline';
11	 *   script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:;
12	 *   connect-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'self'; form-action 'self';
13	 *   base-uri 'none'; object-src 'none'
14	 *
15	 * (app/api/site/[slug]/[[...path]]/route.ts, and a byte-identical copy in
16	 * app/api/preview/[id]/[[...path]]/route.ts). There is no database, no
17	 * accounts, no payments, no CDN and no remote anything. lib/agent.ts spells the
18	 * same constraints out to the model.
19	 *
20	 * So a feature only earns a place in FEATURES if the finished, published site
21	 * genuinely does the thing the label says. Everything a customer will
22	 * reasonably ask for and that we CANNOT do is in NOT_OFFERED instead, named out
23	 * loud with the real reason and a real alternative — not hidden, and never
24	 * shown greyed-out behind an invented upgrade. The design system's rule is that
25	 * a screen which says "this does not exist, here is what you have instead" is
26	 * better than one that looks operable and is not; NOT_OFFERED is that rule as
27	 * data.
28	 *
29	 * ## The one thing that IS server-backed
30	 *
31	 * Forms. lib/site-forms.ts answers `POST /__forms/<name>` on a PUBLISHED site's
32	 * own origin — which is us, because proxy.ts rewrites `<slug>.kodely.site` into
33	 * the site route — stores the submission, and emails it to the owner. The page
34	 * itself stays completely static: a plain `<form method="post">` is a
35	 * NAVIGATION, so `connect-src 'none'` is untouched and `form-action 'self'` did
36	 * not have to be widened by a character.
37	 *
38	 * Two caveats travel with that, and both are in `caveat` below rather than in
39	 * small print:
40	 *   - It works once the site is PUBLISHED. submitSiteForm() refuses anything
41	 *     whose project has no publishedAt, and the in-editor draft preview is
42	 *     served from a different route entirely, so a form in the preview does
43	 *     nothing when submitted.
44	 *   - There is no mailing-list integration behind any of it. A "keep me posted"
45	 *     form collects addresses into the owner's submissions inbox. It does not
46	 *     subscribe anybody to anything.
47	 *
48	 * ## Adding a feature later
49	 *
50	 * Append to FEATURES. `id` is stable (it travels in analytics and in saved
51	 * answers), `description` is one true customer-facing line, `caveat` is
52	 * mandatory the moment the honest description needs a "but", and `fragment` is
53	 * the prose that lands in the build brief. Nothing else in the wizard needs to
54	 * change — the UI groups by `category` and the brief is assembled from
55	 * `fragment` in list order.

## Summary

**Setup note**: dashboard auth couldn't be reached (no credentials, and creating one is prohibited), so I built a temporary unauthenticated route (`app/tmp-wizard-preview/page.tsx`, outside all forbidden paths) to render both modals directly, drove them with `javascript_exec`/DOM measurement (screenshots aren't available in this headless pane), and deleted the route before finishing. `git status` confirms no leftover files and edits confined to `components/wizard/InlineWizard.tsx` and `components/templates/TemplatePickerModal.tsx`.

### Bug 1 — overflow / double scrollbar (root cause, empirically confirmed)

Two independent, additive causes, both in code I own (Modal.tsx's `<dialog>` was never touched):

1. **No height budget tied to the dialog's actual space.** The stage-content region used `max-h-[min(56vh,30rem)]`, sized against the viewport in isolation. The native `<dialog>` has no explicit height/overflow of its own, so it falls back to the UA default (`overflow: auto`, `max-height: calc(100% - Npx)` of viewport). When the wizard's real total (header + rail + that region + footer) exceeded that clamp, the **dialog itself** started scrolling as a second container around the first — verified: at 1280×600 the Features stage showed `dialog.scrollHeight(601) > clientHeight(560)` *and* the inner region overflowing simultaneously.
2. **A second, subtler leak, independent of (1).** Every `sr-only` radio (category chips, look cards, tone chips) is `position: absolute` with no positioned ancestor. Its containing block became the `<dialog>` itself (`dialog:modal` is `position: fixed` in the UA sheet), so its off-screen hypothetical position pierced straight through both `overflow-hidden` and `overflow-y-auto` wrappers and inflated the dialog's own scrollable area — confirmed via `dialog.scrollTop` being draggable to 71px even after fix (1), dragging the header off-screen.

**Fix** (both files): the stage content is now wrapped in `flex max-h-[max(8rem,calc(100dvh-18rem))] flex-col overflow-hidden relative`, with only the stage-content div as `flex-1 min-h-0 overflow-y-auto`; `relative` anchors the sr-only radios locally. Verified `dialog.scrollHeight === dialog.clientHeight` and `scrollTop` frozen at 0 across every stage, at 1280×900, 1280×700, 1280×600, 375×700, and 812×375.

**TemplatePickerModal had the identical bug** (confirmed: 637 vs 560 at 600px height) — fixed identically in both its gallery stage (search/filter now `shrink-0`, grid `flex-1 min-h-0 overflow-y-auto`) and intake stage (single scroller, same height formula), each with `relative` added (intake nests a palette-swatch radio grid).

### Bug 2 — Features stage icon grid

Replaced the checkbox-row list with a responsive icon-card grid (`FEATURE_ICONS`/`NOT_OFFERED_ICONS` lookup maps in `InlineWizard.tsx`, lucide-react icons, safe `Sparkles`/`Info` fallbacks). Used **native CSS container queries** (`@container` / `@sm:` / `@xl:`) rather than viewport breakpoints, since the modal's width is capped independently of the browser window — verified 1/2/3 columns kick in correctly at container widths 297px/472px/611px. Every card keeps the checkbox (now `aria-label`led) plus border+tint selected state, and every existing caveat sentence is unchanged verbatim. Note: `lib/features.ts` gained a `list-filter` feature mid-task (not my edit — pre-existing/concurrent change in the shared working tree); I added its icon (`ListFilter`) too.

### Fix 3 — logo pipeline

Traced fully and **confirmed genuinely connected, no bug**: `answers.logo` → `finish()`'s `logoDataUrl` → `Composer.tsx acceptWizard()` → `CreateFlow.tsx run()` → `POST /api/generate`'s `image` field → `lib/agent.ts` attaches it as real vision content, gated to `attempt === 1` only. Rewrote the copy to state both truths plainly instead of leading with only the negative: it now opens with "Kodely genuinely looks at the file itself... and matches the site's palette and character to what it sees," then the caveat ("What it can't do is put that file on the finished page...") — kept exactly as strong, not softened.

**Verification**: `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint app lib components --max-warnings=0` both pass with zero output. Everything above was confirmed live in-browser via DOM/computed-style measurement (screenshots unavailable in this environment); nothing was left unverified.
